source.title: Lessons Learned from a Unifying Empirical Study of Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning (PETL) in Visual Recognition
source.authors: Zheda Mai; Ping Zhang; Cheng-Hao Tu; Hong-You Chen; Quang-Huy Nguyen; Li Zhang; Wei-Lun Chao

record.file_problem: The supplied title differs slightly from the paper title in the text; otherwise the full text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how stochastic depth affects held-out classification accuracy, a related test of explicit regularization and generalization performance. It does not test the specific claim versions’ interventions or measures.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates PEFT accuracy and discusses over-fitting, but does not report a training–test error gap, random-label fitting, or the specific methods and measurements in V1–V8. Appendix Figure 11 reports the effect of turning drop path on; the paper describes this as regularization. Other reported accuracy comparisons do not directly measure a version’s named behavior.
record.test_reason: The study compares PEFT methods and tests stochastic depth during pretrained ViT fine-tuning. None of its results tests V1–V8: stochastic depth drops transformer blocks rather than applying the dropout intervention in V6; parameter-budget sweeps do not establish the width and zero-training-error conditions in V2. References to capacity and inductive bias provide interpretation rather than tests of those versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors interpret PEFT as combining sufficient learning capacity with effective regularization and recommend nonzero drop path for low-shot training. This is an interpretation of downstream accuracy comparisons, rather than a direct measurement of overfitting. They also conclude that tuned PEFT methods perform similarly but make complementary predictions, and that weight-space ensembling can give full fine-tuning an advantage over PEFT in distribution-shift robustness.
record.recipe_differences: Pre-trained ViT transfer learning with PEFT and AdamW; uses stochastic depth and task-specific fine-tuning rather than the original versions’ setups.
record.method_sensitivity: Drop path rate affects accuracy; dataset domain similarity and available training data affect which PEFT methods compare favorably.

fits_no_version.finding: Turning on stochastic depth improves accuracy for the plotted PEFT methods on low-shot VTAB-1K; Figure 11 reports gains of 1.15–2.51 percentage points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nonzero stochastic depth can improve held-out accuracy during low-shot PEFT of pretrained vision transformers.

record.problems: The drop path gains are presented in a figure without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The study does not report training error alongside test error for this result.
record.rows_left_out: Other accuracy comparisons concern PEFT method performance or distribution shifts and do not measure a behavior named by V1–V8 or the training–test gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out performance under the same architectures and recipes.
Network widening beyond the width needed for zero training error and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers trained from scratch, including the role of learned local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning; using AdamW alone supplies no comparison.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce large-batch penalties.
Dropout's effect on held-out error, training-set-size dependence, underfitting, and joint removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparison with other generalization measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply. Other PEFT accuracy, parameter-budget, ensemble, and distribution-shift comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out and do not measure the interventions or relationships named by V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same recipes.
Width sweeps of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks across the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks trained from scratch.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under the specified tuning regimes.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout specifically; the paper tests drop path (stochastic depth), not dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with training–test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: All methods (aggregate statement)
rows.operation_detail: Turned on drop path (stochastic depth) compared with the default rate of 0.
rows.note: The authors state that all methods benefit from nonzero drop path; the figure shows gains by method, but values are not stated in text.
rows.check: The accuracy improvement is observed, but it cannot establish any listed version. Specify drop-path rate 0.1 versus 0, and restrict the subject to the PEFT methods plotted in Figure 11. The supplied figure text includes numerical gains ranging from 1.15 to 2.51 percentage points, so 'figure only' overlooks available values. This aggregate should be split into method-specific rows if retained.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
